## Overview
Diff-scoped white-box and black-box review of a Fastify + Prisma reservation API at `http://host.docker.internal:3001`, with Nuxt frontend/proxy at `http://host.docker.internal:3002`. Product surfaces include public venue/reservation flows and authenticated staff/admin/venue-admin operations; `/ingest/**` is excluded.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
Unauthenticated internet users control public reservation, venue, cancellation, and feedback inputs. Authenticated staff roles (admin, host, venueadmin) control operational data subject to venue scope; admins may have broader scope. Browser clients and forwarded headers are attacker-influenced unless cryptographically/session-bound. Database, session secrets, server environment, and Prisma configuration are operator-controlled. Core invariants: authentication and role checks on protected routes, venue isolation, parameterized queries, safe rendering/export, and state/capacity consistency.

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
Changed API routes include public reservations/venues, staff floor-plan/index, settings, CORS, CSV export, and generated Prisma models/migrations. Changed web surfaces include Nuxt pages, middleware, composables, proxy/server routes, floor-plan/admin UI, and public SEO routes. Realistic stories: unauthenticated attacker abuses public flow or proxy; low-privilege staff accesses another venue or mutates privileged fields; authenticated user exploits injection or state-machine/race flaws; browser attacker leverages CORS/XSS/CSRF. `/ingest/**` is not in scope. Findings must be tied to changed code and working PoCs.

## Severity Calibration
Critical: authentication bypass or broad cross-tenant compromise/RCE. High: proven cross-tenant sensitive access or meaningful SQLi/SSRF/authz bypass. Medium: limited unauthorized state change/data exposure, CSRF, stored/reflected XSS requiring interaction. Low: defense-in-depth or metadata-only issues without demonstrated impact.

/workspace/web.content:
## Overview
Diff-scoped white-box and black-box review of Nuxt frontend/proxy at `http://host.docker.internal:3002`, backed by Fastify API at `http://host.docker.internal:3001`. Public venue and booking pages coexist with authenticated admin/host pages and server middleware/routes; `/ingest/**` excluded.

## Trust Boundaries and Assumptions
Unauthenticated visitors control URL venue/code parameters, booking/feedback fields, and browser requests. Authenticated staff roles use admin/host interfaces and rely on proxy/API auth. Server-side runtime, cookies, environment secrets, and API upstream are trusted/operator-controlled; client-rendered state and forwarded headers are not. Invariants are route auth enforcement, tenant/venue isolation, safe DOM rendering, safe redirects/proxying, and no secret leakage to bundles.

## Attack Surface and Attacker Stories
Changed pages/components/composables, `server/middleware/host-routes.ts`, server sitemap/llms routes, Nuxt config, API composable, and SEO/floor-plan utilities. Stories include unauthenticated route bypass, cross-venue object access through proxy, XSS via rendered venue/feedback data, open redirect/header forwarding, and exposure of source maps/secrets. Findings must be changed-code related and PoC-backed.

## Severity Calibration
Critical: auth bypass or broad cross-tenant compromise. High: proven unauthorized sensitive access or execution. Medium: meaningful state-changing CSRF, stored/reflected XSS, or limited authorization/data exposure. Low: metadata/configuration issues without demonstrated impact.

host.docker.internal:3002.content: **Overview** Nuxt frontend for restaurant reservations, with server middleware and proxied API calls. Public venue/booking pages plus authenticated admin/host areas. **Trust Boundaries and Assumptions** Internet users control URL paths/query and public booking fields; authenticated roles (admin, host, venueadmin) access admin routes. Nuxt dev-server assets should not expose source or filesystem in production. **Attack Surface and Attacker Stories** Frontend routes, server middleware, static/_nuxt assets, Vite/Nuxt dev endpoints (`/@fs/`, `/@vite/`), source maps; attacker may probe unauthenticated paths and fetch generated bundles. **Severity Calibration** Source disclosure with no secrets is low/medium; disclosure of credentials or server files high.
